## Study Overview

The study keeps mirrored-pair positions, seven-point match context, and rollout settings visible so the reader can see the method before any result summary.

## Why This Study Exists

The goal is to compare engine behavior under a narrow, repeatable protocol. The study does not claim that one engine is stronger, and it does not turn a private fixture run into a final public conclusion [@bms-fixture-methodology].

## Methodology Summary

- Use mirrored pairs.
- Keep the position set fixed.
- Record the same settings for every batch.
- Separate raw output from luck-adjusted summaries.

## Mirrored Pairs

Each pair compares the same position from opposite seating or mirrored perspective so the analysis can check whether the engine response is stable across equivalent views.

## Seven-Point Match Context

The seven-point match setting matters because cube and checker choices can change once score pressure enters the picture.
